01

THE CHALLENGE

Each store had a different business and product range to serve.

The work was to turn each client's brief into its own online store, with a design that reflected the approved direction and a shopping experience that worked across screen sizes. The stores needed to be clear, usable, and ready for customers to browse and purchase.

02

MY PROCESS

Design first. Build after client approval.

01

Understand the brief

I use the design brief and client emails to clarify the goals and requirements.

02

Design in Adobe XD

I create the initial visual direction and share it with the client for review.

03

Get approval

I confirm the design with the client before development begins.

04

Build in Shopify

I customize the client's purchased theme, refine sections, and set up payment gateways.

03 / THE SOLUTION

Approved design, translated into Shopify.

I use Liquid to customize selected sections and apply UI/UX and SEO standards during implementation. I also check that each store responds well on mobile and consider page speed as I build.

04 / THE RESULT

3 distinct Shopify stores

Each site was built to closely match its approved XD design, with a 99% match as my target, mobile responsiveness, and speed considered. No sales or traffic figures are claimed.

02 / SELECTED CLIENT PRODUCTS

Print and event design,
made for the real world.

Selected client projects across business cards, event displays, and magazine advertising. Client names and dates are shown where available; project dates are omitted.

01

THE CHALLENGE

Client-specific artwork, ready before event day.

TLG clients requested packaging, booth, tabletop, and event materials for their own needs. The designs had to follow each client's print guide and arrive in time for production. Some pieces needed to be printed about a week before an event so they could be shipped.

02

MY PROCESS

Build to spec, check the file, protect the deadline.

I start with the client brief and emails, then create effects in Photoshop and vector elements and text in Illustrator. I follow the exact print-guide dimensions, allow for bleed, set the artwork to CMYK, and proofread the copy. I export the approved artwork as a print-ready PDF or JPG and keep production and shipping time in view.

03 / THE SOLUTION

Print-ready files for distinct client projects.

The selected work includes KMicro business cards, Kyūdō and TriCore IMS banner stands, a ROM Infinite Mobile Apps magazine page, and a 21st Century Programming table skirt.

04 / THE RESULT

Positive client feedback.

Clients were very happy with the results. Event work helped attract participants to an event. I do not have attendance figures to report.
